newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major-will not offset tax cuts with new rises.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major-will not offset tax cuts with new rises.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday he did not anticipate replacing any new tax cuts with other tax increase elsewhere.

"I am not anticipating that we would replace one tax reduction with another tax increase but I cannot, and it would not be proper, to try and anticipate every event that may occur in the future or what choices a future Chancellor will make," he told reporters at a news conference launching the Conservative Party's manifesto for the May 1 election.

I cannot conceive, except in the most exceptional circumstances that cannot be forseen at the moment, that we would need to increase general tax levels in the next Parliament given our public expenditure plands and outlook for the economy," Major said.

Major said over the past three or four years the government has made more significant reductions in public expenditure than any previous government at any stage. "And we will continue to retrench public expenditure," he said.
